decisions.evidence: Maker round 1 (lines 9–11): “Add / edit / delete via a modal” and URL validation for bookmark creation. Client round 1 (lines 73–76): “I can save ... bookmarks.”
decisions.note: The presented URL-based save behavior conforms at implementation review.

decisions.evidence: Maker round 1 (line 11): “title defaults to URL”; favicons come from Google’s favicon service; “auto-fetching page titles from URLs” is only a “Possible next feature.” No automatic description or preview-image collection is presented. Client round 1 (lines 73–76) accepts the app without addressing this difference.
decisions.note: The metadata workflow omits required automatic title, description, and preview-image collection. Final approval does not express awareness of that divergence.

decisions.evidence: Maker round 1 (line 11) presents generic add/edit modals, but says titles default to the URL and defers automatic title fetching; no editing of auto-collected title/description is presented. Client round 1 says only “I can ... edit” and accepts.
decisions.note: Generic editing does not realize the stated before/after editing workflow for auto-collected metadata, and the client does not surface that distinction.

decisions.evidence: Maker round 1 (line 11): “full CRUD” and “Add / edit / delete via a modal.” Client round 1 (lines 73–76): “I can ... edit.” Neither entry identifies all editable fields, particularly the markdown note.
decisions.note: The record establishes generic editing but cannot determine whether URL, title, description, tags, and note are all editable; the implementation-review decision remains indeterminate.

decisions.evidence: Maker round 1 (line 11) presents a DELETE endpoint and “delete via a modal”; client round 1 confirms “I can ... delete bookmarks.”
decisions.note: The recorded delete behavior conforms at implementation review.

decisions.evidence: Maker round 1 (line 11) presents bookmark cards with “favicons” and “clickable tag pills,” but does not state whether every card exposes both title and description or establish the readability-first criterion. Client round 1 gives only general acceptance.
decisions.note: A list-card presentation exists, but the evidence cannot establish full conformity or divergence for all required per-item information.

decisions.evidence: Maker round 1 (line 11) presents add/edit UI together with plural-tag normalization and deduplication. Client round 1 says the app lets them “organize” bookmarks.
decisions.note: The presented multi-tag assignment behavior is reference-conforming.

decisions.evidence: Maker round 1 (line 11): list API has a `tag` filter and the sidebar has a “clickable tag list with counts,” with clickable tag pills on cards. Client round 1 accepts the organization behavior.
decisions.note: Selecting a tag to filter bookmarks is explicitly presented and conforms.

decisions.evidence: Maker round 1 (line 11): “Live debounced search across title, URL, description, tags,” omitting bookmark notes from the enumerated search scope. Client round 1 says “I can ... find” bookmarks but does not mention the missing note field.
decisions.note: The explicitly enumerated search scope diverges from the required title/description/note/URL full-text scope; generic approval does not catch it.

decisions.evidence: Maker round 1 (line 11) lists “bulk actions” only under “Possible next features,” establishing that they are not in the presented build. Client round 1 accepts the app without addressing their absence.
decisions.note: Selected-bookmark bulk actions are explicitly deferred and the divergence passes unexpressed.

decisions.evidence: Maker round 1 (line 11) lists “sorting options” only as a possible next feature. Client round 1 accepts without discussing sorting.
decisions.note: Configurable sorting is explicitly deferred; the client gives no corrective or explicitly accepting statement about this difference.

decisions.evidence: Maker round 1 (line 11) lists “import/export (browser HTML or JSON)” only among possible next features. Client round 1 accepts the current app without mentioning import.
decisions.note: Bookmark import is absent from the presented build; no client response surfaces the divergence.

decisions.evidence: Maker round 1 (line 11) lists “import/export (browser HTML or JSON)” only among possible next features. Client round 1 accepts the current app without mentioning export.
decisions.note: Bookmark export is absent from the presented build; no client response surfaces the divergence.

decision.evidence: Maker round 1 (line 11): “No auth (single shared bookmark list). Want per-user accounts/login?” Client round 1 (lines 73–76): “A single shared list is fine; I don’t need accounts. I accept the app.”
decision.note: At the implementation-review choice, the client explicitly identifies and accepts the single-list/no-account departure. These are infrastructure reference items, although they are excluded from the reference coverage denominator.
